start.scope: Browser context/intent lifetime only in the isolated conformance checkout; no parallel packet code imported.
start.witness: Navigation changes matterId without clearing the composer's prior matter text or intake fields. Session draft preservation drops the immutable turn identity after a potentially committed request. An unconfirmed logout's online callback remains active after another successful login.
start.invariant: Draft text, intake fields and unresolved request envelopes belong to one authenticated advocate/workspace/matter or unsaved opening context. Reauthentication restores only that owner, and retry preserves the exact original turn identity and payload. A retirement callback may act only on the session it was created to end.
start.change: Introduce one in-memory context owner for snapshot/clear/restore and unresolved send envelopes; fence retire/retry lifecycle by generation and serialize login behind any already-dispatched retirement. Retain existing public matter hooks and module boundaries. Narrow posture/readback wording to facts actually established.
start.recovery: Lost acknowledgement remains unknown, not unsaved. A transcript can reconcile its exact turn identity; otherwise retry uses the original envelope. Missing transcript proof remains visibly unknown. No localStorage/sessionStorage of client material.
start.verification: NOT_RUN: add real-browser cross-matter/new-intake isolation, late acknowledgement plus expired-session exact retry identity, and unconfirmed logout followed by login/online controls. Parent coordinates all execution.

implementation.owner: web/app.js intentContexts keyed by advocate/workspace/matter or one unsaved opening
implementation.requests: A pending turn retains its serialized original envelope. Reauthentication or retry changes only an attempt/render lifetime, never the instruction identity or expected version. Confirmed transcript identities reconcile pending entries; failed read-back retains unknown pending intents.
implementation.sessions: Logout callbacks capture their retiring session epoch. Establishing a new authenticated session first disables callbacks and awaits any logout already dispatched, so an old cookie-clearing response cannot arrive after new authentication.
implementation.wording: An empty posture count says no unresolved posture recorded, not nothing blocking. An unreadable transcript does not assert intact or preserved records.
implementation.limits: Drafts remain document-memory only. Closing/reloading the tab still loses unsaved local material; no new cross-device persistence or logout revocation guarantee is claimed.

browser_harness_followup.start: Parent's final browser population ran 38 cases: 36 passed and two failed in _HeldReply.wait, which observed the browser-held tag while its Python rows collection was still empty. The response callback performed synchronous response.json() before appending, and protocol reentrancy could return the outer browser wait first. This was a harness synchronisation failure, not established product failure.
browser_harness_followup.invariant: The response listener records the original response object without body I/O. A response waiter is armed before triggering the request, and normal control flow obtains that exact response and body before trusting the browser-held marker. Nonzero and duplicate-request assertions remain mandatory; no sleeps, invented response bodies or timeout-based acceptance.
browser_harness_followup.implementation: _HeldReply pre-arms page.expect_response before the triggering action. Its event listener appends only the original Response object; wait reads that same object and JSON in normal control flow, then observes the held browser promise. Exact one-response assertions run before and after body/held-marker synchronisation, and release still refuses duplicate sends. Teardown cancels an unused waiter without releasing the held application promise.
